about: funground's small table of Hindustani ragas and talas for learners (S-115, contract A8, D-062). Each fact was checked against the published sources cited with it, in October 2026. Where sources disagree, the most common form is given and the notes say so. Sargam: S r R g G m M P d D n N (lower-case r g d n are komal, M is tivra Ma), ' for the octave above, a comma for the octave below. Tala beats count from 1; the sam is beat 1.

ragas.name: Yaman
ragas.aroha: N, R G M P D N S'
ragas.avaroha: S' N D P M G R S
ragas.pakad: N, R G R S P M G R S
ragas.time: evening: the first prahar of the night, about 6 to 9 pm
ragas.notes: Uses tivra Ma only (with shuddha Ma as well it is Yaman Kalyan). The aroha often skips Sa and Pa (SwarGanga gives N, R G M D N S'). Wikipedia's text puts it at 9 pm to midnight; Tanarang and SwarGanga give the first prahar of the night. The pakad is the one Wikipedia gives; Tanarang's main phrases differ, as pakads do between teachers.

ragas.name: Bhupali
ragas.aroha: S R G P D S'
ragas.avaroha: S' D P G R S
ragas.pakad: G R S D, S R G P G D P G R S
ragas.time: evening: the first prahar of the night, about 6 to 9 pm
ragas.notes: Pentatonic: no Ma and no Ni. Deshkar uses the same five swaras; Bhupali rests on Ga and the lower part of the scale, Deshkar on Dha and the upper part. Wikipedia gives 7 to 9 pm.

ragas.name: Bilawal
ragas.aroha: S R G P D N S'
ragas.avaroha: S' N D P D n D P m G R S
ragas.pakad: G R G P D n D P m G R G P D N S'
ragas.time: morning: the first prahar of the day, about 6 to 9 am
ragas.notes: This is Bilawal as usually taught, Alhaiya Bilawal (Parrikar treats the two names as one raga): Ma is left out going up, and komal Ni is touched only coming down (D n D P). Shuddha Bilawal, a separate raga, uses all seven shuddha swaras and no komal Ni. SwarGanga gives a twisting aroha, S G R G P D N S'. Its swaras are the same set as Khamaj and Desh.

ragas.name: Khamaj
ragas.aroha: S G m P D N S'
ragas.avaroha: S' n D P m G R S
ragas.pakad: n D m P D m G
ragas.time: night: the second prahar, about 9 pm to midnight
ragas.notes: Shuddha Ni going up and komal Ni coming down; Re is left out going up. SwarGanga gives 6 to 9 pm. Desh and Bilawal use the same set of swaras.

ragas.name: Asavari
ragas.aroha: S R m P d S'
ragas.avaroha: S' n d P m g R S
ragas.pakad: R m P n d P
ragas.time: late morning: the second prahar of the day, about 9 am to noon
ragas.notes: This is the shuddha Re form taught in Bhatkhande's system; Ga and Ni are left out going up. An older form with komal Re (Komal Rishabh Asavari, in Bhairavi thaat) is also sung, and some use both. A more typical descent is S' R' n d P d m P g R S. Wikipedia's pakad is m P d m P g R S. NCERT gives 11 am to 1 pm.

ragas.name: Bhairavi
ragas.aroha: S r g m P d n S'
ragas.avaroha: S' n d P m g r S
ragas.pakad: S n, S r g m g r S
ragas.time: morning: the first prahar of the day, about 6 to 9 am; by custom it ends a concert, at any hour
ragas.notes: In practice singers often add other swaras (Mishra Bhairavi). The vadi is disputed: Ma and Sa (Tanarang, Darbar, and Parrikar, who calls it traditional); Wikipedia gives Ma or Pa with Sa; R. Jha gives komal Dha and komal Ga (quoted by Parrikar). The pakad is Parrikar's.

ragas.name: Todi
ragas.aroha: S r g M d N S'
ragas.avaroha: S' N d P M g r S
ragas.pakad: g M d N d M g r g r S
ragas.time: late morning: the second prahar of the day, about 9 am to noon
ragas.notes: Miyan ki Todi. Pa is usually left out going up (Bor, via Wikipedia; ITC SRA) and used sparingly coming down; Tanarang and Darbar print Pa in the aroha but say it is generally skipped. Without Pa at all it is Gurjari Todi. The pakad is Parrikar's core phrase. ITC SRA gives 10 am to 1 pm.

ragas.name: Marwa
ragas.aroha: D, N, r G M D N S'
ragas.avaroha: S' N D M G r S
ragas.pakad: D M G r G M G r S
ragas.time: sunset: the end of the fourth prahar of the day, about 4 to 7 pm
ragas.notes: No Pa. Tanarang gives 3 to 6 pm and ITC SRA 4 to 7 pm. Wikipedia's aroha is N, r G M D N r' S'. V. N. Patwardhan argued for Dha and Ga as vadi and samvadi (quoted by Wikipedia). The pakad is Bhatkhande's, as Wikipedia quotes it.

ragas.name: Durga
ragas.aroha: S R m P D S'
ragas.avaroha: S' D P m R S
ragas.pakad: m P D m R D, S
ragas.time: night: the second prahar, about 9 pm to midnight
ragas.notes: Pentatonic: no Ga and no Ni. Darbar alone gives Pa as the vadi. Tanarang's avaroha is S' D P D m R S D, S, and it says Pa is not a resting note coming down. A different Durga in Khamaj thaat is almost never heard now. The pakad is Tanarang's.

ragas.name: Desh
ragas.aroha: S R m P N S'
ragas.avaroha: S' n D P m G R S
ragas.pakad: R m P D m G R P m G R
ragas.time: night: the second prahar, about 9 pm to midnight
ragas.notes: Shuddha Ni going up, komal Ni coming down; Ga and Dha are left out going up. The descent is often sung S' n D P D m G R G N, S. Wikipedia's infobox says late night; its text, Tanarang and Darbar say 9 pm to midnight. The same swaras as Khamaj and Bilawal. The pakad is Parrikar's.

ragas.name: Deshkar
ragas.aroha: S R G P D S'
ragas.avaroha: S' D P D G P G R S
ragas.pakad: P D G P S' D D P P D G P G R S
ragas.time: morning: the first prahar of the day, about 6 to 9 am
ragas.notes: The same five swaras as Bhupali, with the vadi and samvadi the other way round. It lives in the upper half (P D S') and comes down to Dha. SwarGanga's avaroha is S' D P D P G R D, S; IndianClassicalMusic.com gives 7 to 10 am. The pakad is from Tanarang's main phrases.

talas.name: Ektaal
talas.notes: Spellings vary: Tu or Tun at beat 5; Ta (NIOS, UW) or Tin (SwarGanga) at beat 8; TiRaKiTa is also written TirKit or Terekite. 'Tun Na Kat Tin' is also common.

talas.name: Rupak
talas.notes: Unusually, the sam is a wave (khali), not a clap. Books number the claps differently: here beat 4 is the second sign and beat 6 the third; the UW page numbers them 1 and 2.
